newsitem.title: UK: Millennium not in Metropole talks.
newsitem.headline: Millennium not in Metropole talks.

text.p: Millennium & Copthorne Plc said on Wednesday that it was not in talks to acquire the Metropole chain of hotels from Lonrho Plc.

"Millennium & Copthorne did look at Metropole hotels but negotiations are not going on at the moment," a spokesman said, adding that newly-floated Millennium was looking at a number of potential acquisitions in the sector.

Conglomerate Lonrho, in the throes of a three-way split, said last month that it had received interest from potential buyers for its Metropole and Princess hotels and as a result had delayed a planned flotation of the properties.
Glasgow-based hotels and casino group Stakis Plc is seen as the front-runner to buy the Metropole, a four-star chain with five sites in Britain.
A spokeswoman for Stakis, which has some 46 UK hotels, declined to comment on the rumours on Wednesday.

Saudi billioniare investor Prince al-Waleed bin Talal is believed to be negotiating the purchase of the Princess hotels for $300 million. The 10 Princess hotels are located in the U.S., the Caribbean and Mexico.
The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that Lonrho expected to complete the sale of the two chains for more than 650 million stg within a fortnight. There was no immediate comment from Lonrho.
